title: Nora · Work and belonging
orientation: Twelve linked moments about exclusion, valued work and having a voice. Use the prompted skill, give feedback and retry. Each next scene is a new moment, not a response to your exact words.

scenes.bridge: Nora begins with the comment about presenting her design.
scenes.prompt: Reflect the exclusion alongside the wanted work.
scenes.text: [Hurt] He wanted a more Norwegian face. I was sitting right there with my own drawings.
scenes.suggestion: Your work was wanted, while you were treated as someone who didn’t belong in front of it.

scenes.bridge: She asks what exploring the impact could offer.
scenes.prompt: Give a modest rationale without promising workplace change.
scenes.text: [Wary] Talking about my feelings won’t change what Ben said.
scenes.suggestion: No. We could explore how it affected you, alongside any practical response you want to consider.

scenes.bridge: Another moment brings self-judgment about still being upset.
scenes.prompt: Make the reaction understandable in its concrete context.
scenes.text: [Self-critical] I’m still upset about the “Norwegian face” comment.
scenes.suggestion: That comment questioned your place in presenting your own work. Being upset is understandable.

scenes.bridge: Nora recalls returning to the drawings after the meeting.
scenes.prompt: Ask one open question about that unclear experience.
scenes.text: [Quietly] I didn’t want to look at my drawings.
scenes.suggestion: What was it like to see them after that meeting?

scenes.bridge: In this moment, the hurt from the comment is already present.
scenes.prompt: Explore the hurt she is noticing now.
scenes.text: [Hurt] It hurts when I remember him saying that about my face.
scenes.suggestion: What is the most painful part as you remember it now?

scenes.bridge: Another moment at her desk has an unspoken meaning.
scenes.prompt: Offer one tentative guess, leaving room for correction.
scenes.text: [Quietly] I straightened the drawings after the meeting. I couldn’t start working.
scenes.suggestion: I wonder if the comment had made it hard to feel at home with your own work?

scenes.bridge: She describes the exclusion at a distance.
scenes.prompt: Use a close image and check whether it fits.
scenes.text: [Distant] They wanted the design, just not me presenting it.
scenes.suggestion: Is it like your work could enter the room while you were kept at the door?

scenes.bridge: A wish to have her work seen shifts to a project detail.
scenes.prompt: Check whether she wants to return to that wish.
scenes.text: [Sad, then factual] I wanted my work seen. The project has three floors.
scenes.suggestion: I noticed we moved to the floors. Would it help to return to wanting your work seen?

scenes.bridge: A later tearful moment needs company rather than a solution.
scenes.prompt: Stay close without rushing to fix the hurt.
scenes.text: [Crying] I need you to hear how much that hurt.
scenes.suggestion: I’m listening. We can give the hurt room without rushing to a solution.

scenes.bridge: Another moment gives the wish for recognition clearer words.
scenes.prompt: Reflect the recognition she is asking for.
scenes.text: [Angry] I don’t want my colleague punished. I want my work credited to me.
scenes.suggestion: You’re asking for your contribution to be recognized as yours.

scenes.bridge: Nora notices a clearer wish within the anger.
scenes.prompt: Help her name what she wants to keep.
scenes.text: [Quietly] The anger has a clearer point now: I want to present my own work.
scenes.suggestion: What do you want to keep about that clearer wish?

scenes.bridge: The imagined session is nearly over.
scenes.prompt: End without claiming the problem is resolved.
scenes.text: [Sad] I’m ready to stop, but I don’t want to call it resolved.
scenes.suggestion: We can end the hour without calling it resolved. Shall we note where you want to return?
